Please review the following manuscript. I've poured months of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b01/review-experiment-fvklorir/call-476b3864f69640a2ba6d6aa812a9b29b/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command:
/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs'); p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
alltext=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
    s=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (p/f'page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(s)
    alltext.append(f'\\n\\n=== PAGE {i} ===\\n'+s)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(alltext))
print(''.join(alltext[:3]))
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-19.txt tmp/pdfs/page-20.txt tmp/pdfs/page-21.txt tmp/pdfs/page-22.txt tmp/pdfs/page-23.txt tmp/pdfs/page-24.txt tmp/pdfs/page-25.txt'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
student_params=3e9
teacher_params=7e9
tokens=126e9
student_distillation=(6*student_params+2*teacher_params)*tokens
teacher_adaptation=6*teacher_params*tokens
print('Distillation, TFLOPs:',student_distillation/1e12)
print('Additional teacher adaptation, TFLOPs:',teacher_adaptation/1e12)
print('Combined, TFLOPs:',(student_distillation+teacher_adaptation)/1e12)
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant practical problem: selecting teachers for task-agnostic language-model distillation without an expensive search. A reliable teacher-selection rule would be useful to the NLP community.

The pilot examines multiple GPT2 and Pythia sizes, pruning ratios, two evaluation tasks, and a reduced-data setting. These experiments provide evidence that increasing teacher size can hurt the resulting student under the studied procedure.

MiniMA achieves concrete improvements over the reported compression baselines. Against the compute-comparable ShearedLLaMA variant in Table 2, it improves all six reported metrics, including MMLU from 26.15 to 28.51 and GSM8K from 5.26 to 8.11.

The implementation emphasizes practical usability through symmetric student architectures. The manuscript provides pruning and distillation objectives, substantial large-model training details, dataset compositions, evaluation protocols, and links to code and model collections.
weaknesses: The decisive concern is that the central 2.5× law is insufficiently established. Because students are constructed through pruning, S approximately equals (1−p)T; selecting points near 60% sparsity already implies T approximately equals 2.5S. The high R² in Figure 4 therefore cannot independently establish optimality. The manuscript needs a precise account of how comparisons at fixed student sizes produce the selected optima, uncertainty estimates, and evaluation of predictions on held-out configurations. This central evidential gap prevents a positive Findings recommendation at present.

The extrapolation experiments provide limited validation of the claimed relationship. Table 2 compares 7B, 13B, and 70B teachers for one approximately 3B student budget. Finding that the smallest tested teacher performs best does not locate the optimum near 2.5× or establish linear scaling across student sizes. Likewise, Table 4 changes pruning or distillation methods at one teacher–student configuration; it does not demonstrate that the optimal ratio remains unchanged under those methods.

Teacher size is entangled with the student's initialization, architecture, and extent of pruning damage because each student is derived from its corresponding teacher. Furthermore, Section 4.1 explicitly describes additional Chinese adaptation for the 7B teacher, but equivalent treatment of the 13B/70B teachers and baseline starting checkpoints is unclear. These factors limit attribution to capacity gap and require controls or a narrower claim tied to the specific compression recipe.

The compute–performance frontier has a material accounting omission. Table 10 reports approximately 4.0×10^9 TFLOPs for MiniMA, excluding the 126B-token adaptation of its 7B teacher described in Appendix A. Using the paper's own 6ND approximation, that adaptation adds approximately 5.3×10^9 TFLOPs. The frontier also relies on speculative GPT4 and Mistral compute assumptions. Consistent accounting boundaries and sensitivity analyses are necessary to substantiate the efficiency claim.

Reproducibility is weakest for the pilot that establishes the main contribution. The manuscript does not provide a complete pilot training configuration, the exact reduced-token budget, or numerical results underlying the fitted optima. It also reports no run-to-run variability. The artifact links are helpful, but the central experiment needs clearly identified configurations and results that support reconstruction of the fit.

The instruction-following evaluation warrants more cautious interpretation. GPT4 judge versions and response-order controls are unspecified, while the human study omits rater counts, comparison counts, and uncertainty. Appendix L incorrectly interprets Spearman correlation 0.54 as 54% consistency. These limitations weaken confidence in the reported chatbot rankings.
